Lab 1 · Exercise 2 · SC-5009

Secure and Monitor
AI Workloads

Learn how to lock down your AI workload infrastructure — connect Key Vault securely, review network risks, and switch on audit logging so nothing slips through undetected.

Azure Key Vault Microsoft Foundry Log Analytics 4 Tasks · ~35 min
In this exercise
00Create Azure Resources & Foundry 01Connect Key Vault to Foundry 02Identify Network Security Risks 03Enable Diagnostic Logging
What is this exercise about? Your AI workloads don't just depend on the model itself — they rely on supporting services like Azure Key Vault (for safely storing API keys and passwords) and network controls (for keeping traffic away from the public internet). In this exercise you'll set all of that up, then turn on monitoring so you can see exactly what's happening inside your AI environment.
🏗
Task 0
Create Azure Resources & Foundry
Before you can secure anything, you need to create the three services that power this lab: a Resource Group (the folder that holds everything), an Azure Key Vault (your secure secrets store), and a Log Analytics Workspace (where logs will be collected). Then you'll set up your Microsoft Foundry project on top.
💡 What is Azure Key Vault?
Think of Key Vault as a secure safe for your cloud environment. Instead of putting API keys and passwords directly in your app’s code (risky!), you store them in Key Vault and your app retrieves them on demand. Only authorised identities can open the safe.
💡 What is a Log Analytics Workspace?
It’s a central place where Azure collects and stores log data from your services. Think of it as a searchable logbook — when something happens in your Foundry resource, the workspace records it so you can investigate later.
1
Open Microsoft Edge and go to https://portal.azure.com. Sign in using the credentials from the Info tab (ⓘ) in your lab panel — use the Cloud Express Pass username and Temporary Access Pass. In the search bar, type Resource groups and select it.
2
Click + Create. In the resource group name field, type rg-foundry-lab. Select your subscription and choose any region. Click Review + create.
3
Review the summary — confirm the name is rg-foundry-lab — then click Create to deploy your resource group.
4
In the search bar, type Key vaults and select it. Click + Create to start creating your Key Vault.
5
Select rg-foundry-lab as the resource group and enter a globally unique name for your vault. Review the summary and click Create.
💡The vault name must be unique across all of Azure — if it's taken, add your initials or numbers to make it unique.
6
In the search bar, type Log Analytics Workspaces and select it. Click + Create.
7
Select rg-foundry-lab as the resource group, enter a unique workspace name, then click Review + Create → Create.
8
Open a new tab and go to https://ai.azure.com. Sign in with your lab credentials. Enable the New Foundry toggle, then create a new project. Expand Advanced options and select rg-foundry-lab as the resource group. Click Create and wait for setup to finish.
9
Once the project is ready, go back to the Azure Portal and open rg-foundry-lab. You should now see all four resources: Key Vault, Log Analytics Workspace, Foundry, and Foundry project.
🔑
Task 1
Connect Azure Key Vault to Microsoft Foundry
Right now, your Key Vault and Foundry project don't know about each other. In this task you'll introduce them — but carefully. Rather than giving Foundry full admin access, you'll use least-privilege access: granting only the minimum permissions needed. Then you'll connect the vault inside your Foundry project.
💡 What is a Managed Identity?
A Managed Identity is like an ID badge that Azure automatically creates for a service like Foundry. Instead of embedding a username and password in your app to access Key Vault, Azure handles authentication automatically. It's more secure because there are no credentials to accidentally leak.
💡 What is the Key Vault Secrets User role?
It's a built-in Azure role that gives read-only access to secrets in Key Vault. Foundry only needs to read secrets — not create or delete them — so this is exactly the right role: just enough access, nothing more.
1
Return to the Azure Portal. Open Resource groups and select rg-foundry-lab. Then click on your Key vault resource.
2
In the left sidebar, click Access control (IAM). Then click + Add → Add role assignment.
3
On the Role tab, search for Key Vault Secrets User and select it. This gives read-only access to secrets — exactly what Foundry needs. Click Next.
4
On the Members tab, select Managed identity under Assign access to. Click + Select members. In the flyout, change the dropdown to Foundry — your Foundry resource will appear. Select it and click Select.
5
Confirm the Foundry resource is listed as a member. Click Review + assign twice to complete the role assignment.
6
Switch to https://ai.azure.com. Disable the New Foundry toggle. When prompted, click Continue without feedback.
📝You need to disable New Foundry to access the Management Center where connected resources live.
7
Scroll to the bottom of the left sidebar and click Management center. Under Resource in the sidebar, click Connected resources. Click + New connection.
8
In the dialog that opens, search for Key Vault and select it from the results.
9
The Add an Azure Key Vault dialog will open. Your vault will appear. Under Authentication, confirm Account managed by identity is selected — this uses the managed identity you just gave access to. Click Add connection.
10
You will see a green Connected badge appear next to your vault. Click Close — Key Vault is now securely linked to your Foundry project.
✅You've successfully granted Foundry least-privilege access to Key Vault using its managed identity and connected the vault as a project resource.
⚠️
Task 2
Identify Network Security Risks for AI Workloads
Before you lock things down, you need to know where the gaps are. In this task you'll review the current network configuration of both your Key Vault and Foundry resource — looking for anything that's open to the public internet when it shouldn't be.
💡 Why does network exposure matter for AI workloads?
If your Key Vault is accessible from any IP on the internet, anyone with valid credentials can reach it from anywhere — including attackers who've stolen those credentials. In production you'd lock it down so only your trusted virtual networks can reach it. No private endpoint and public access open = a risk that needs addressing.
1
Go back to the Azure Portal. Open Resource groups and select rg-foundry-lab.
2
Click on your Key vault resource. Inside Key Vault, go to Settings → Networking. On the Firewalls and virtual networks tab, review the three access levels. Note which one is currently selected.
⚠️In production, you would change this to Specific virtual networks and IP addresses or Disable public access and use a private endpoint instead.
3
Click the Private endpoint connections tab. You'll see No results — meaning all traffic to this Key Vault currently travels over the public internet instead of a private, isolated network path.
4
Click back to return to the resource group. This time click on the Foundry resource (type shows as "Foundry", not "Foundry project").
5
In the Foundry sidebar, expand Resource Management and click Networking. On the Firewalls tab, note the current setting is All networks — meaning any device on the internet can reach your Foundry resource.
⚠️This is the risk: All networks = unrestricted public access. In production, change this to Selected Networks and Private Endpoints or Disabled.
✅You've identified two network risks: Key Vault has no private endpoint and Foundry allows unrestricted public access. You now know exactly what to lock down in a real environment.
📊
Task 3
Enable Diagnostic Logging in Microsoft Foundry
Securing your infrastructure is great — but you also need visibility. If something goes wrong (or someone tries something suspicious), you need logs to investigate. In this task you'll configure diagnostic settings on your Foundry resource to capture audit logs and ship them to the Log Analytics workspace you created in Task 0.
💡 What are Diagnostic Settings?
Diagnostic settings are how Azure resources "talk" to monitoring services. By enabling them, your Foundry resource will automatically send logs and metrics to your Log Analytics workspace in real time. You can then query those logs, set up alerts, and build dashboards — without any custom code.
💡 What does an Audit log capture?
Audit logs record who did what and when — things like who accessed the resource, what API calls were made, and whether any configuration changed. For AI workloads this is critical: you need to know if someone is making unusual requests to your model endpoints or changing security settings.
1
Still on the Foundry resource page, look in the left sidebar under Monitoring and click Diagnostic settings. The arrow in the previous screenshot pointed to it.
2
The Diagnostic settings page shows all the available log categories (Audit Logs, Request and Response Logs, etc.) and currently says No diagnostic settings defined. Click + Add diagnostic setting.
3
Fill in the form:

• Name: foundry-diag
• Under Logs tick Audit Logs
• Under Destination details tick Send to Log Analytics workspace
• Select your subscription and the workspace you created

Click Save.
✅You've configured diagnostic settings to capture audit logs from your Foundry resource and forward them to Log Analytics for monitoring and investigation.
🎉

Exercise Complete!

You've secured the infrastructure layer of an AI workload — connecting secrets management with least-privilege, reviewing network exposure, and switching on audit logging. These are the foundations of a well-governed AI environment.
